title: One Point Lesson - Barscreen Cleaning (Suction Screen) (OPL-CT-7801-01)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-CT-7801-01 - Barscreen Cleaning (Suction Screen).

Equipment: CT-7801 (COOLING TOWER CELL FAN), Discipline: Process / Operations, Area: 7800 - COOLING TOWER SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: SEQ-7801 (SIL 1), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-7801.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains barscreen cleaning (suction screen) for CT-7801 (COOLING TOWER CELL FAN) in the COOLING TOWER SYSTEM. A clogged barscreen starves the circulating water pumps and fouls the fill, reducing cooling for the whole unit. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Obtain the correct operating permit and brief the shift team before the task.
- Precaution 2: Confirm hazardous fluids are isolated / inerted as required by procedure.
- Precaution 3: Beware of flammable, hot, or high-pressure fluids; wear the correct PPE.
- Precaution 4: Never defeat a safety interlock or trip without an authorised override permit.
- Precaution 5: Have emergency actions and communications ready before starting.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: Operating procedure & P&ID
- Tool 2: Radio / communication with panel
- Tool 3: Gas detector (O2 / LEL) as required
- Tool 4: Correct PPE for the fluid handled
- Tool 5: Sample containers & PPE for sampling
- Tool 6: Permit-to-work documentation

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Rake the SS304 barscreen every shift on the round
- Step 1 - Check: Permit valid & briefed
- Step 2 - Action: Remove leaves, debris and biological growth
- Step 2 - Check: Parameter within limit
- Step 3 - Action: Check the differential level across the screen
- Step 3 - Check: Interlock status confirmed
- Step 4 - Action: Dispose of debris correctly and log the cleaning
- Step 4 - Check: Change logged on DCS
- Step 5 - Action: Report rapid re-fouling to water treatment
- Step 5 - Check: Handover to next shift

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: Routine barscreen cleaning on operator round | Likely Cause: Normal debris accumulation | Action: Raked barscreen clear, checked differential level
- Symptom: Scheduled fan gearbox oil change | Likely Cause: Routine - oil sample acceptable | Action: Drained and refilled ISO VG 220, replaced breather
- Symptom: VSHH-7802 vibration alarm on CT-7801 fan | Likely Cause: Leading-edge erosion on one FRP blade caused imbalance | Action: Inspected blades, re-balanced fan, vibration normalised

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: A clogged barscreen starves the circulating water pumps and fouls the fill, reducing cooling for the whole unit.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-7801: e.g. VSHH-7802 trips at > 9 mm/s - never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-7801 before working on CT-7801.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
